source.title: Dubai is Building a $35BN Mega Airport

notes: (originally filed as case 'b1m_dubai_al_maktoum_intro') Full visual teardown of the opening 3-minute comparison sequence (00:02 to 03:15). Measured shot holds and overlay timestamps directly from high-resolution video frames.

marks.source_words: How big can an airport be?
marks.why: Opening hook statement overlaid large in kinetic typography over opening cinematic shot.

marks.source_words: London Heathrow in comparison to Manhattan
marks.why: Satellite map comparison highlighting Heathrow footprint overlaid against Manhattan outline.
Map graphic swaps to Dubai International DXB footprint for immediate scale comparison.
Satellite overlay scales up showing Al Maktoum airport engulfing Manhattan map.

marks.source_words: less an airport and more a city with some planes
marks.why: Metaphorical comparison; editor cuts to render architectural footage without visual text.

marks.source_words: more than 260 million passengers a year
marks.why: Key metric displayed as prominent yellow stat overlay over terminal render.
Rapid-fire spec callout overlaid on aerial layout render.
Rapid-fire spec callout continued over roof detail shot.
Freight spec callout overlaid over ground-level entrance shot.
Project cost climax shown as centered bold monetary stat tag.

marks.source_words: most ambitious piece of transport infrastructure
marks.why: Superlative commentary allowing the cinematic render montage to breathe.
High-level thematic statement accompanied by wide regional satellite view.

marks.source_words: Or at least that's the plan
marks.why: Presenter direct-to-camera intro transition; intentionally clean of graphics.

marks.source_words: just how big it really is
marks.why: Conversational presenter delivery setting up the comparative analysis.
Dual split-screen satellite comparison illustrating total land boundaries.
Qualitative distinction expanding on the satellite visual without adding clutter.
Re-reference to Manhattan; map graphic is already established on screen.
First column in an expanding 4-way comparative split showing LHR passenger statistics.
Airport name is integrated directly into the split column header alongside the metric mark.

marks.source_words: more than 100 million passengers a year
marks.why: Second comparative column added to the live comparison split for ATL.
Third comparative column added to the split screen for Ethiopia's BIA.
Final fourth column revealing Al Maktoum towering over the prior benchmarks.

marks.source_words: more than double the passenger volume
marks.why: Mathematical summary of the 4-way split that is already fully visible on screen.

marks.source_words: three out of every four Americans
marks.why: Infographic showing a 75% demographic ratio fill over the US map.

marks.source_words: That's a hell of a lot of people
marks.why: Punchy on-screen text emphasis capping off the population comparison.

marks.source_words: cargo capacity and that is absolutely enormous
marks.why: Introductory transition to freight topic; b-roll of Emirates A380 shown without text.
Yellow metric tag stating target cargo capacity.

marks.source_words: Hong Kong International Airport currently handles the most cargo
marks.why: Satellite map overlay isolating HKG cargo hub.

marks.source_words: sits at around 5 million tons annually
marks.why: Metric callout displaying current world #1 cargo tonnage.
Rapid-fire bullet text popping up on presenter's lower third.

marks.source_words: by cargo and by runway capacity
marks.why: Sequential lower-third statement update listing the next record.
Sequential lower-third statement update for terminal record.

marks.source_words: largest footprint of any airport on the planet
marks.why: Final sequential lower-third statement in the record list.
Humorous punchline delivered directly to camera by the host; deliberately uncluttered.
